title: Hold the acrylic sheet down and peel its protective film off by the tab
instruction: Hold the white acrylic sheet down with your left hand. With your right hand, pinch the brown paper tab on the far edge of the film and peel the film off by lifting it up and back toward you, then drop the film in the blue basket on the right.
context: Every new acrylic sheet, screen or appliance panel comes with a protective film that people peel off by a tab while the other hand holds the light part down: pulled straight back, the tab tears, and pulled without a hand on the part, it lifts with the film.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions are centres in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, heights above the table. Cutting mat: a 22 x 24 cm green self-healing cutting mat (24 cm along y), 3 mm thick, fixed, at (0.33, -0.05). Sheet: an opal white cast acrylic sheet, 15 x 20 cm (20 cm along y), 3 mm thick, 105 g, lying loose on the mat at (0.33, -0.05). Film: brown kraft masking paper printed "PROTECTIVE FILM" on the sheet's right half (y from -0.15 to -0.05), cut across x into four strips 3.75 cm wide and 10 cm long (1.5 mm thick, 5 g each), joined to each other (see below). Each strip is stuck along its edge nearer the robot by a 100 mm long band of low-tack removable tape under it (start 6 mm wide, narrowed or widened until calibrated): it comes unstuck when its far edge is pulled straight up with 1.6 N (a 0.06 N m twist, 37.5 mm from the glued edge), about as hard as it takes to tip the loose sheet up, and holds at least 8 N pulled along the sheet. The strips are joined at each cut by 19 mm wide clear tape on the top face, 100 mm long, centred on the cut, edges touching (holds 8 N or more). The sheet's left half is bare. Tab: a folded kraft card tab, trimmed to 4 g, 3 cm wide (along y), 2.5 cm tall and 3 mm thick, standing on the film's far edge at (0.40, -0.10), free to turn on its fold. The fold is a 30 mm wide kraft paper hinge with a perforated crease, calibrated to tear at 4 N (3.5 to 4.5 N, with a spring scale pulled along the sheet and at 45 degrees up). Basket: a blue open-weave plastic basket, 12 x 16 cm (16 cm along y) and 6.9 cm tall, fixed, on the robot's right at (0.235, -0.265), off the mat. Nothing else is on the table. Calibration with a 10 N spring scale on spare coupons: lift a glued strip straight up at its far edge, it lets go at 1.6 N (1.4 to 1.8 N, 5 of 5); pulled along the sheet it holds 8 N; and with nothing holding the sheet the first peel tips or slides it, while a finger on its near left corner keeps it flat. Full steps in the README.
scoring: Positions are centres. A strip counts as peeled once its centre has been 1 cm or more from its place on the sheet (measured on the sheet), and stays peeled. 0 for the rest of the trial once the tab has torn off (its centre 2 cm or more from its fold on the film), or once the sheet's centre has been more than 2 cm from its start or the sheet tilted more than 10 degrees (lifted with the film or dragged), and 0 if it is off the table. Otherwise: 1.0 (success, held 1 s with the film still): all four strips peeled and the centre of every strip and of the tab within 6 cm along x and 8 cm along y of the basket's centre and lower than its rim. 0.5: all four strips peeled, the film not all in the basket. 0.25: two or three strips peeled. 0 otherwise, including doing nothing or peeling one strip.
reset_notes: Make a new film for every trial: 70 g/m2 kraft paper cut into four 37.5 x 100 mm strips, joined by 19 mm clear tape at the cuts, each with its 100 mm low-tack glue band, and a new tab on a perforated paper hinge. Check the batch first with spare coupons and a spring scale: 1.6 N peel per strip, 8 N hold along the sheet, 4 N tab tear. Stand the tab up and lay the film on the sheet's right half. A torn tab or a peeled strip means a new film.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz physics, 20 Hz control. The paper film is four rigid strips 1.5 mm thick and 5 g each (real film: 0.1 mm, under 1 g), joined by free ball joints, and the tab turns on a ball joint. Each strip's glue is a fixed joint that breaks at a 0.06 N m twist or 8 N, with no creep or re-sticking. The tab tears at 4 N. The sheet, mat and strips collide as boxes, the basket as its mesh. The gripper closes with 50 N per pad.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both hands reach over the sheet and the right hovers by the tab, but it never pinches the tab and no strip comes off), demo: 1.0 (success at step 348)
